name: Tax Map
one_liner: An interactive map comparing England's Council Tax with an illustrative annual property tax, area by area.

text.why: Tax-reform debate is usually about averages, not your own home. Tax Map lets you enter a postcode or area, adjust the rate and see the estimated change.
text.take: The methodology and data-attribution documents are published alongside.
build: Shades 296 council areas on a map with yearly or monthly changes, optional Stamp Duty and your own figures. It uses official data from ONS, HM Land Registry and VOA/HMRC and needs no API keys.

who.role: Anyone curious how a property-tax reform could affect a home in England.

start.text: Try the live demo at taxmap.limsight.com and enter a postcode.

caveat: An illustrative scenario, not personal tax advice, and some areas have no estimate. The code is MIT, but data and map assets keep their own licences.

license.scope_text: Use, change and redistribute, commercially too. Keep the notice.

numbers.star_delta_unit: GitHub stars gained in the window, GH Archive events summed to as_of
numbers.method: Star total = the value last checked on GitHub (stars_checked_at) + increases observed via GH Archive since. The 24h · 7d · 30d gains are GH Archive hourly events summed to the reference time (as_of). No score of ours.

images.alt: The Tax Map: a map of England and a Leicester comparison showing an estimated £741 decrease.

notes: This file was produced by the same build, from the same data, as the tesign.com item page. The text is editorial; the numbers are stored observations.
null in the JSON means not observed — never zero. The Markdown writes [unconfirmed] for it.
